name: LaunchPact
tagline: A commitment tool for shipping: you set a launch date, you agree to terms, something keeps you honest about it.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanical part of a launch pact is a deadline, a checklist, and a nagging reminder, and that is a single-session build for any competent agent. The part that actually changes behavior is external: another human who sees you miss the date, or money you forfeit when you do. You can self-host the tracker, but you cannot self-host shame, and a pact you can silently edit at 2am is a to-do list with extra ceremony. Build it if you want the artifact and the audit trail, pay if the enforcement is the product. Details here are thin, so treat the specifics as unverified.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where you define a launch commitment with a hard date, milestones, and stakes, then get scheduled email nudges and a public read-only status page that logs every time you move the goalposts.
requirements: an SMTP or Resend API key in .env if you want reminder emails
somewhere to run a daily cron if you want nudges without leaving your laptop open
whatYouLose: An actual counterparty: nobody else is holding the other end of your pact
Financial stakes, escrow, and payouts, which are the only enforcement most people respond to
Hosted reliability, so reminders stop when your machine or cron does
Mobile push and a polished shame-inducing UI
Any social layer: cohorts, witnesses, public streaks other people can see
moatNotes: Accountability products are worth exactly as much as the other people in them; solo mode is a spreadsheet with feelings.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is being watched. A self-built commitment tracker is enforced by the same person who wants to break the commitment, which is a governance problem no amount of code fixes. Paying also creates a small sunk cost that itself does some of the work, and the hosted version keeps running on the week you stop caring, which is precisely the week it matters.
notes: The tracker is trivial, the enforcement is not: build it only if you already keep promises to yourself.
prompt:
Build a local-first launch commitment tracker called "pact" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/pact.db
- Drizzle for schema and migrations
- Nodemailer for email, config from .env

Data model:
- pact: id, title, description, launchDate, stakesText, witnessEmail, createdAt, status (active | shipped | failed)
- milestone: id, pactId, title, dueDate, completedAt
- amendment: id, pactId, field, oldValue, newValue, reason, createdAt

Behavior:
- A form to create exactly one active pact: title, launch date, up to 8 milestones, free-text stakes, one witness email.
- Dashboard shows days remaining, milestone progress, and an amendment log.
- Editing launchDate or stakes on an active pact is allowed but ALWAYS writes an amendment row and requires a typed reason. Never edit silently, never delete amendments. Display the amendment count prominently next to the countdown.
- Marking shipped requires a URL. Past the launch date with no ship URL, status flips to failed on next cron run.
- A read-only public page at /p/[id] showing title, date, status, milestone progress, and the full amendment log. No auth, unguessable nanoid ids.
- A script scripts/nudge.ts that sends one daily email to the owner and, on missed milestones and on the launch date, to the witness. Run it from cron or GitHub Actions.

Out of scope: accounts, payments, escrow, multi-user pacts, mobile app, analytics, telemetry.

Include .env.example with SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, MAIL_FROM, OWNER_EMAIL, and a README with setup, migration, and cron instructions. Seed one example pact. Keep it under roughly 800 lines of app code.
